hook: Why Young Dickens Cried in Westminster Hall
text: One evening in eighteen thirty-three, a young shorthand reporter crept up a dark court off Fleet Street and dropped a story into a magazine's letter-box. He did not sign his name. Weeks later, in a bookshop, he opened the new issue, and there it was, in print. He walked to Westminster Hall and stayed inside for half an hour, because his eyes were so dimmed with joy and pride that they were not fit to be seen in the street. His name was Charles Dickens.
